---
title: "Perturbation techniques and separation of time scales"
subtitle: "Otto & Day, appendix on perturbation techniques, with PracticalCAS"
engine: julia
---

When a parameter is small (weak selection, rare mutation, weak coupling),
quantities that have no simple closed form can be expanded in powers of it.
When some variables change much faster than others, the fast ones can be set
to their quasi-equilibrium.

```{julia}
using PracticalCAS
@syms x ε
```

## Roots of an equation as a series

At `ε = 0` the roots are 0 and 2; `perturb` corrects each order by order.

```{julia}
rts = perturb(x^2 - (2 + ε) * x + ε, x, ε; order = 3)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
exact = solve(x^2 - (2 + ε) * x + ε, x)
for r in rts
    @assert any(abs(evalf(subs(r - e, ε => 0.01))) < 1e-7 for e in exact)
end
```

## Equilibrium allele frequency under mutation–selection balance

A deleterious allele with selection coefficient `s` arises by mutation at
rate `μ`. In the haploid model the equilibrium solves a quadratic; to first
order in the small mutation rate it is `μ/s`:

```{julia}
@syms q::(0, 1) s::(0, 1) μ::positive
nextq = (1 - μ) * (1 - s) * q / (1 - s * q) + μ * (1 - q)
perturb(numerator(cancel(nextq - q)), q, μ; order = 2)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
pr = perturb(numerator(cancel(nextq - q)), q, μ; order = 2)
@assert any(r -> isequiv(taylor(r, μ, 0, 1), μ / s), pr)
```

## Eigenvalues of a weakly coupled system

Two populations each regulated at rate 1 and 2, exchanging migrants at a
small rate `ε`: the eigenvalues move away from -1 and -2 at second order.

```{julia}
@syms λ
J = [-1 ε; ε -2]
perturb(charpoly(J, λ), λ, ε; order = 2)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
ev = perturb(charpoly(J, λ), λ, ε; order = 2)
@assert any(isequiv(e, -1 + ε^2) for e in ev) && any(isequiv(e, -2 - ε^2) for e in ev)
```

## Separation of time scales: enzyme kinetics

The enzyme–substrate complex `C` forms and dissociates fast compared with the
consumption of substrate `S`. Setting `dC/dt = 0` gives the Michaelis–Menten
rate for the substrate:

```{julia}
@syms S::nonneg C::nonneg k₁::positive k₋::positive k₂::positive E₀::positive
mm = ode(S => -k₁ * S * (E₀ - C) + k₋ * C, C => k₁ * S * (E₀ - C) - (k₋ + k₂) * C)
reduced = only(quasi_steady_state(mm, C))
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
Km = (k₋ + k₂) / k₁
@assert isequiv(reduced.rhs[1], -k₂ * E₀ * S / (Km + S))
```

## A fast resource

Consumers `N` feed on a resource `R` that is supplied at rate `a`, decays at
rate `b` and is consumed at rate `c R N`; the resource turns over much faster
than the consumers reproduce. At the resource's quasi-equilibrium
`R = a/(b + c N)` the consumers follow a single equation with a saturating
growth rate, and settle where `c R = m`:

```{julia}
@syms R::nonneg N::positive a::positive b::positive c::positive m::positive
chemo = ode(R => a - b * R - c * R * N, N => N * (c * R - m))
slow = only(quasi_steady_state(chemo, R))
```

```{julia}
equilibria(slow)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(slow.rhs[1], N * (c * a / (b + c * N) - m))
@assert any(e -> isequiv(e[N], (c * a - b * m) / (c * m)), equilibria(slow))
```
